correctness.rationale: Expanding P−2Q gives the three concurrent line factors; the restricted Q cubics give all equilibria in both directions. Their critical values (or discriminant signs) give the three stated open intervals. Each derivative has two distinct zeros, so at zero discriminant there is a double root, not a triple root. The common point (1/5,−2/5) satisfies Q=1/6−h and contributes exactly two duplicate counts at h=1/6. The interval ordering gives nine exactly in the asserted window and the stated counts 8, 6, and 7 at its lower endpoint, upper endpoint, and just above it. The top-degree factors are three distinct directions and each restricted Q has a nonzero cubic term, ruling out intersections at infinity. On a line x=my+b, the determinant reduces to (P−2Q)_x times the derivative of the restricted Q; determinant zeros thus require a critical value or the concurrent point. The full trace is 5x−5x²+(15/2)y². Its zeros on lines one and two occur at parameter values 0, 1/30, or 1/6 only. For line three, writing c=y+1, positive determinant requires |c|>√13/5 and then 15c²−12c+1>0, so the trace is negative. Consequently no positive-determinant branch can cross the imaginary axis. Independent exact sign brackets at h=1/10 establish 5 saddles, 2 sources, and 2 sinks; the types persist throughout the window.
